title: ork pins a project's slicer contract and checks the pin
findings_note: owner session 2026-10-20 (in slicer): ork sets and checks each tool's pin (adj 97, decided). Owner 2026-10-30: this slice is the slicer pin only; the adj half is its own v1.1 slice behind adjudicate S45. Companion: slicer s387 (relay contract pin, landed).
boundary: **Not in this slice:** the adj pin, `adj contract` and any adj check (the v1.1 slice behind adjudicate S45), any change to slicer or adj, storing a pin in `projects.json`, and serving or translating an older contract.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
ork accepts a fixed set of slicer relay versions (`internal/roles/roles.go:59`, `acceptedContracts = []int{10, 11}`, adj 175). It refuses others at engine start (`internal/engine/engine.go:248-262`) and in doctor (`internal/cli/doctor.go:250-272`). One gap remains: **no project records the version its tools agreed on.** slicer s387 added the pin (`relay_contract` in `.slicer/config.json`, `slicer config relay_contract N`; `ai relay` exits 2 with `contract_mismatch` and prints no text on a mismatch, `slicer/docs/agents.md:712`). ork reads `pinned` (`internal/slicercli/contract.go:90-97`) but never sets a pin, and doctor checks only the project it is run in.

Owner decisions:

- 2026-10-20 (adj 97, `boundary.contract-pin`, decided `ork-sets-checks`): each tool keeps its pin in its own committed config; ork sets and checks the pins. The accepted sets stay as what ork can speak, and a pin must be in ork's set.
- 2026-10-30 (v1.0 session, interactive): this slice does the slicer pin only. The adj half waits on adjudicate S45 and is filed as its own v1.1 slice, so v1.0 does not wait on adjudicate. The 2026-10-26 joint-release gate no longer includes S45. Until the adj half lands, doctor warns and passes on an adj with no `contract` command, and engine start does not refuse.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/slicercli/write.go:33`: `Contract` reads `slicer ai relay --json --root ROOT` and returns the `contract` string, so the first-line text parse goes. Add `SetRelayPin(ctx, root, n)` and `UnsetRelayPin(ctx, root)`, which run `slicer config relay_contract N --root ROOT` and `slicer config relay_contract --unset --root ROOT`.
- `internal/slicercli/contract.go:90-97`: `Validate` keeps its pin check. A `contract_mismatch` tool error (exit 2) comes back as an error that names the pinned and installed versions.
- `internal/cli/daemoncmds.go:70-150`: `ork projects pin NAME --relay N [--json]` and `ork projects unpin NAME [--json]`, beside `list`, `add`, `rm` and `set`; update the usage text at the top of `projects`.
  - It resolves NAME through `registry.Load` (`internal/registry/registry.go:244`) without the daemon, as doctor does, and needs no daemon.
  - It refuses N outside `roles.AcceptedContracts()` with the usage code and runs nothing.
  - It writes the pin only through slicer, never `config.json`.
  - It reports what `slicer ai relay --json --root P` then prints as `pinned`.
- `internal/cli/doctor.go:44-50,290-300,404-420`: `contractCheck` gains a per-project list `{project, pinned, found, ok, error}` over the registered projects (the loop at `doctor.go:296` already reads them without the daemon). A project fails when its pin is outside the accepted set, or its slicer refuses with `contract_mismatch`. The existing global check stays, and adj is not checked (see the adj slice).
- `internal/engine/engine.go:248-262`: engine start refuses a project whose slicer reports `contract_mismatch`, with the error naming both versions and no run record created. The `Contract` first-line call and `CheckContractLine` use the `--json` string instead.
- `internal/cli/cli.go`: the `ork projects` usage lines and the doctor line (`cli.go:117`).
- `docs/boundaries.md:33-48`, `docs/design.md:1423-1434` (the "exit 3" in the pin sentence is wrong: slicer exits 2, `slicer/docs/agents.md:712`; fix it here), `docs/guide.md:63-68` (the contract line in doctor), `:94` (the other `projects` commands), `:367` and `:397` (the command list), CHANGELOG.
- `testdata/cli/slicer/`: recorded `slicer ai relay --json` with `pinned` null (`relay-v11.json` exists), equal, and the `contract_mismatch` error object with exit 2. Re-record the exit code in `internal/slicercli/contract_test.go:62` and `internal/cli/fix_round1_test.go:12`, which fake exit 3.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
Fake CLIs replay recorded outputs (decision 0047).
- `ork projects pin p --relay 11` runs exactly `slicer config relay_contract 11 --root P` and exits 0.
- `--relay 9` and `--relay 12` (not accepted) exit 2, run no tool, and the message lists the accepted set.
- A NAME not in the registry exits 2 and runs no tool. If the slicer call fails, the error names slicer's message.
- `ork projects unpin p` runs exactly `slicer config relay_contract --unset --root P`.
- `ork doctor --json` with one registered project pinned at 11 and slicer printing 11 lists it ok. With slicer refusing `contract_mismatch` (exit 2) it fails and names both versions. With no pin it is checked only against the accepted set, as today.
- Engine start on a project whose slicer reports `contract_mismatch` (exit 2) refuses with an error naming both versions and creates no run record.
- Two projects with different pins are each checked with their own `--root` (the two-project test the 2026-10-20 review asked for).
- Existing doctor and engine tests stay green with no pins set.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the red tests against recorded outputs, then the code.
2. Record the equal-pin and `contract_mismatch` outputs once from a scratch project under `.scratch/` (never a real repo), and keep them in `testdata/cli/slicer/`.
3. Update the docs listed in Files. Do not paste slicer's contract text; refer to commands.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l .` are clean. SPDX headers. No new dependency.
- `slicer check` and `adj lint` pass.
- [HUMAN CHECK] With the rebuilt `~/bin/ork` (S198) and slicer 1.17.0: `ork projects pin` on a scratch project, then `ork doctor` lists it ok. Set the pin to a version slicer does not print: doctor fails naming both versions. Then `ork projects unpin` clears it.
